quote: 1. People who succeed in the stock market also accept periodic losses, setbacks, and unexpected occurrences. Calamitous drops do not scare them out of the game.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 2. Go for a business that any idiot can run - because sooner or later, any idiot probably is going to run it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 3. Companies that have no debt can't go bankrupt.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 4. This is one of the keys to successful investing: focus on the companies, not on the stocks.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 5. A correction is a wonderful opportunity to buy your favorite companies at a bargain price.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 6. The trick is not to learn to trust your gut feelings, but rather to discipline yourself to ignore them.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 7. Investing without research is like playing stud poker and never looking at the cards.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 8. The best stock to buy may be the one you already own.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 9. A stockholder without information is not going to stay a stockholder for long.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 10. If you can follow only one bit of data, follow the earnings.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 11. The average person can concentrate on a few good companies, while the fund manager is forced to diversify. By owning too many stocks, you lose this advantage of concentration.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 12. What the stock price does today, tomorrow, or next week is only a distraction.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 13. I think we should follow five or six companies and maybe own one or two.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 14. Far more money has been lost by investors preparing for corrections, or trying to anticipate corrections, than has been lost in corrections themselves.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 15. We see the latest correction not as a disaster, but as an opportunity to acquire more shares at low prices. This is how great fortunes are made over time.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 16. Everyone has the brainpower to make money in stocks. Not everyone has the stomach.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 17. When yields on long-term government bonds exceed the dividend yield of the S&P 500 by 6 percent or more, sell your stocks and buy bonds.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 18. You have to let the big ones make up for your mistakes. In this business, if you're good, you're right six times out of ten. You're never going to be right nine times out of ten.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 19. It takes remarkable patience to hold on to a stock in a company that excites you, but which everybody else seems to ignore. You begin to think everybody else is right and you are wrong. But where the fundamentals are promising, patience is often rewarded.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 20. With small companies, you are better off to wait until they turn a profit before you invest.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 21. In business, competition is never as healthy as total domination.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 22. In this business, you always find out too late when you're wrong.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 23. All the math you need in the stock market you get in the fourth grade.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 24. The person that turns over the most rocks wins the game. And that's always been my philosophy.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 25. A successful stockpicker has the same relationship with a drop in the market as a Minnesotan has with freezing weather—you know it's coming, and you're ready to ride it out, and when your favorite stocks go down with the rest, you jump at the chance to buy more.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 26. The worst thing you can do is invest in companies you know nothing about. Unfortunately, buying stocks on ignorance is still a popular American pastime.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 27. Find a company that no analyst has ever visited, or that no analyst would admit to knowing about, and you've got a double winner. When I talk to a company that tells me the last analyst showed up three years ago, I can hardly contain my enthusiasm.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 28. Never fall in love with a stock—always have an open mind.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 29. There's no use diversifying into unknown companies just for the sake of diversity. A foolish diversity is the hobgoblin of small investors.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 30. Long shots almost always miss the mark.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 31. You get recessions, you have stock market declines. If you don't understand that's going to happen, then you're not ready, you won't do well in the markets.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 32. There is always something to worry about. Avoid weekend thinking and ignore the latest dire predictions of newsletter writers.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 33. This is a stock picker's market, and stock pickers are made, not born.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 34. A lot of great fortunes in the world have been made by owning a single wonderful business.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 35. There's nothing wrong with cash. It won't help you, but it won't hurt you either, and it lets you sleep well at night.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 36. Know what you own, and know why you own it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 37. Owning stocks is like having children – don't get involved with more than you can handle.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 38. Everybody knows that if you're a lousy shopper, you're not going to do as well in the mall as if you're a sharp shopper. Why should you be any different in the stock market?
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 39. You only need a few good stocks in a lifetime to make a lot of money.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 40. Just because a stock goes down doesn't mean it can't go down more.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 41. Gentlemen who prefer bonds don't know what they're missing.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 42. Corporations, like people, change their names for one of two reasons: either they've gotten married, or they've been involved in some sort of unsavory activity they're trying to cover up.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 43. Behind every stock is a company. Find out what it's doing.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 44. The first task of the bargain hunter is to narrow the field and separate the solid prospects from the ones that are counting on hopes, prayers, and miracles.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 45. People go to the library and they do incredible research on a microwave oven. And then they'll go out and spend $10,000 on a stock because they heard a tip on the bus.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 46. If you're prepared to invest in a company, then you ought to be able to explain why in simple language that a fifth grader could understand, and quickly enough so the fifth grader won't get bored.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 47. Just because you buy a stock and it goes up does not mean you are right. Just because you buy a stock and it goes down does not mean you are wrong.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 48. In the long run, it's not just how much money you make that will determine your future prosperity. It's how much of that money you put to work by saving it and investing it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 49. There is no shame in losing money on a stock. Everybody does it. What is shameful is to stay in a stock, or worse, to buy more of it, when the fundamentals are deteriorating.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 50. You can lose money in a very short time but it takes a long time to be really good at investing.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 51. Every once in a while, the market does something so stupid it takes your breath away.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 52. Selling your winners and holding your losers is like cutting the flowers and watering the weeds.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 53. You can't see the future through a rear-view mirror.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 54. It's easier to figure out what's going to happen to earnings and the fundamentals of a company over the next five years than it is to figure out what's going to happen to the stock over the next three months.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 55. The key organ is the stomach, not the brain.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 56. Big companies have small moves, small companies have big moves.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 57. The simpler it is, the better I like it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 58. If you like the store, chances are you'll love the stock.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 59. The tortoise beats the hare in the market too, and, all in all, it's much easier being a tortoise, once you've made your peace with the plodding pace.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 60. In stocks, as in romance, ease of relationship is often directly proportional to distance kept.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 61. The real key to making money in stocks is not to get scared out of them.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 62. Nobody can predict interest rates, the future direction of the economy, or the stock market. Dismiss all such forecasts and concentrate on what's actually happening to the companies in which you've invested.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 63. If you spend more than 13 minutes analyzing economic and market forecasts, you've wasted 10 minutes.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 64. Stop listening to professionals!
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 65. The stock market demands conviction as surely as it victimizes the unconvinced.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 66. Insiders might sell their shares for any number of reasons, but they buy them for only one: they think the price will rise.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 67. When you sell in desperation, you always sell cheap.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 68. Invest in what you know.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 69. You have to keep track of where the future growth is coming from and when it's likely to slow down.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 70. Never invest in any company before you've done the homework on the company's earnings prospects, financial condition, competitive position, plans for expansion, and so forth.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 71. Although it's easy to forget sometimes, a share is not a lottery ticket, it's part ownership of a business.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 72. Never invest in any idea you can't illustrate with a crayon.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 73. The best way to handle a situation in which you love the company but not the current price is to make a small commitment and then increase it in the next sell-off.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 74. My diaries are full of such missed opportunities, but the stock market is merciful—it always gives the nincompoop a second chance.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 75. In the long run, a portfolio of well-chosen stocks and/or equity mutual funds will always outperform a portfolio of bonds or a money-market account.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 76. Time is on your side when you own shares of superior companies.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 77. The extra courage and conviction that come from understanding the company can make the difference between losing your shirt in a bear market and cleaning up in a bull market.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 78. If you're an investor, you're concerned with what will happen to your assets. If you're a trader, you're concerned with what will happen to the next guy.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 79. The p/e ratio of any company that's fairly priced will equal its growth rate.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 80. There's no reason to think brains alone will help you play the stock market. If that were true, a lot of professors would be a lot richer than they are.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 81. Frequently, there is no correlation between the success of a company's operations and the success of its stock over a few months or even a few years, but eventually, there is a 100 percent correlation between the success of the company and the success of its stock.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 82. A stock market decline is as routine as a January blizzard in Colorado. If you're prepared, it can't hurt you.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 83. Everyone has the brainpower to follow the stock market. If you made it through fifth-grade math, you can do it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 84. The more right you are about any one stock, the more wrong you can be on all the others and still triumph as an investor.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 85. When management owns stock, then rewarding the shareholders becomes a first priority, whereas when management simply collects a paycheck, then increasing salaries becomes a first priority.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 86. Charts are great for predicting the past.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 87. What you want to see on a balance sheet is at least twice as much equity as debt, and the more equity and the less debt the better.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 88. You don't have to be a genius to make money on Wall Street. You just have to be more disciplined than the average investor.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 89. Absent a lot of surprises, stocks are relatively predictable over ten to twenty years. As to whether they're going to be higher or lower in two or three years, you might as well flip a coin to decide.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 90. Markets go down, sometimes they go down a lot. If you are not ready for this, you shouldn't own stocks.
speaker: Peter Lynch
